title: Ang 721–722: Tilang begins
hook: as the Word comes, Lalo, on ang 722
tomorrow: how long does water stay in a cracked clay pot?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bairari: two pages, and a servant who keeps their goodness when slandered. Small. The week ends on a voice that won't be made small.
screen: `SMALL.` → `A VOICE THAT WON'T BE MADE SMALL.`

segments.voice: Some messages get softened before they're sent. A friend checks the wording, and the hard sentence becomes a gentler one. In Tilang, on ang 722, Guru Nanak refuses the edit. He tells his friend Lalo: as the Master's word comes to me, so I speak it. And what comes is an army. The hymn speaks of violence against ordinary people, so a gentle note for anyone listening with kids: it names harm without describing it.
screen: `THE SOFTENED MESSAGE.` → `AS THE WORD COMES, LALO.` → `AND WHAT COMES IS AN ARMY.`

segments.voice: Tilang opens on ang 721 with Guru Nanak praying in Persian words: one plea I make to you; listen, Creator. Then, on ang 722, the hymn to Lalo, whom tradition remembers as a carpenter the Guru chose to stay with. In paraphrase: the invader has come from Kabul with a wedding party of sin, demanding a bride by force. Modesty and goodness have gone into hiding, and falsehood struts about. The hymn names what the people suffered, plainly, and doesn't flatter the powerful. That's truth to power: the true thing about strength used badly, said in the words that came, unedited. And since this is the week's last day, look at how it led here. Within, the fragrance in the flower. Plain prayers, Dhanna's lentils. Quiet strength, a hand on the forehead. Strength, a beat that never drops. Tender, said once in the morning. Small, two pages and whole. Each one honest. Tilang carries that honesty out into the street. Truth to power.
screen: `ONE PLEA: LISTEN, CREATOR.` · `AS THE WORD COMES, LALO.` · `A WEDDING PARTY OF SIN.` · `THE WEEK: EACH ONE HONEST.` · then, large: `TRUTH TO POWER.`

segments.voice: Take a pen and write one true sentence you've been softening, for your eyes only, and don't edit it. Then set the pen down, rest your hands, and sit with the sentence as it is.
Ang 721. Where Tilang begins: one plea to the Creator, and a page later, the hymn to Lalo.
Truth to power: speak as the word comes, without the edit. A week, done; fifteen thirty-three.

chat.says: uncle told navi at dinner she should quit her job after the wedding. bebe shut him down. rude or right?
options: Right, if she said it plainly; Guru Nanak said the true thing out loud.
Rude. Elders should keep the peace at dinner, whatever gets said.
Right only if she'd waited and told him privately, after the wedding.
chat.meaning: On ang 722 Guru Nanak speaks as the Word comes and names what power did. Truth to power is the true thing, not the comfortable one.
